s1.syndrome_frame: a postmenopausal woman with a long-standing, progressively enlarging breast mass associated with skin ulceration
salient_findings: mass is hard, non-tender, and mobile
skin breakdown with mild exudation and bleeding
key_facts: 56-year-old postmenopausal woman
right breast mass noted for more than 1 year
mass has gradually enlarged
mass is hard in texture
mass is non-tender
mass is mobile
skin ulceration with mild exudation and bleeding
4.5 × 5.5 cm irregular, poorly defined, hard mass
mass is at the 1 o’clock position in the right breast, 2.5 cm from the nipple
no palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
left breast is normal
breast ultrasound and MRI classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
serum breast tumor markers are within normal limits

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, consistent with patient's age and presentation

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: skin ulceration and rapid progression are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: skin involvement and nipple-areolar complex location are typical

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rapid growth and large size are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Metaplastic breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: poorly defined mass and skin ulceration are possible features of this aggressive subtype
